title: VPC traffic zones Terraform module: edge/core subnets, NAT/IGW, service endpoints, and routing profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module that models a two-tier VPC network fabric (edge vs core traffic zones) with explicit subnet allocation per AZ, configurable NAT/IGW egress profiles, VPC endpoints (gateway and interface), and route table profiles. The module should be opinionated enough for private deployments to provide consistent networking topology across customers while allowing configurability for transit/centralized egress patterns and service endpoint needs.
design_notes: Module exposes variables for cidr_blocks per AZ, public/private subnet counts, nat_profile (none | nat-gateway | managed-nat-EIP | centralized-transit), and endpoint_map (service->type + options)
Routing profiles: 'edge' (public subnets + IGW), 'core' (private subnets + NAT/central egress), and 'service-only' (private subnets with interface endpoints only)
Prefer AWS managed NAT Gateway by default for simplicity; support option to deploy shared NAT instances for cost-sensitive customers via 'managed-nat-EIP' profile

VPC endpoints: create gateway endpoints for S3/Dynamo and optional interface endpoints for SSM/EC2 messages/Secrets Manager; each interface endpoint gets a security group managed by module with minimal egress rules
Route table ownership: module returns route table IDs for each profile so consumer modules (e.g., eks, ecs) can attach subnet associations deterministically

Health checks: implement automated egress health monitoring using CloudWatch alarms on NATGatewayBytesOut/Errors and a Lambda-driven remapping to alternate route table (standby NAT) on sustained failure; expose a 'health_check_enabled' flag
Tagging and naming conventions follow org standard: redwood:env, redwood:component, redwood:owner
State and upgrade considerations: avoid renaming resources during 0.x->1.0 bumps; provide migration docs for terraform state mv commands where resource addresses change
tasks: Define module inputs/outputs and document variables in README
Implement subnet allocation logic with support for explicit AZ mapping and automatic CIDR splitting
Implement NAT profiles with optional centralized transit gateway integration
Create VPC endpoint creation templates (gateway and interface) and SG rules for interface endpoints
Implement route table templates for each routing profile and export route table IDs
Add CloudWatch alarms and Lambda runbook for automated egress failover
Write Terratest-based integration tests that bring up module with minimal config in CI
Add GitHub Actions workflow: terraform fmt/validate/plan/apply (apply in ephemeral test account only), and policy checks (Sentinel/OPA)
acceptance_criteria: Module can be instantiated with a minimal set of variables and creates a VPC with separate edge and core subnet groups across 3 AZs
Public subnets have IGW route; private subnets have NAT or transit routes according to selected nat_profile
Gateway endpoints for S3 created when enabled; interface endpoints created for specified services and associated security groups present
Module outputs include vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, route_table_ids_by_profile, and endpoint_ids
Health check feature triggers CloudWatch alarm and Lambda remaps route table association to standby NAT in integration test (simulated via CloudWatch metric put)
Terratest suite passes and GitHub Actions runs terraform validate/plan without errors
Upgrade path documented: step-by-step state migration for any resource address renames and recommended minimal downtime procedure
rollout_plan: Merge module into infra-modules repo behind feature-flag branch
Run full terratest in sandbox account (GitHub Actions) and capture plan diffs
Publish v0.1.0 tag and share with internal platform teams for dogfooding (one customer env)
Collect feedback, iterate to v1.0 with any API changes and migration docs
Announce availability and add module to internal templates and bootstrap tool
upgrade_strategy: Follow semantic versioning for public inputs/outputs: breaking changes go in major bump
If route table or subnet resource addresses change, provide terraform state mv commands in CHANGELOG and automated RFR script
Maintain deprecated variables for one minor release with clear warnings in plan output
Test upgrade path in a cloned sandbox VPC before recommending to customers
tests: Terratest: create/destroy cycle with nat_profile=nat-gateway and endpoint_map minimal
Unit tests: validate variable validation helper functions (cidr splitting) using go test
CI policy checks: terraform-compliance and checkov scans on module
Manual validation: spin up EKS nodegroup consuming private_subnet_ids and verify outbound connectivity and S3 access via gateway endpoint
